Every ND treatment shpws genome richness= 1 expected because each RDRP hit maps to one contig so each ND record contributes one unique contig in the joined table.

1 Calulating VOTUs

create using RvANI90 (Average nucleotide identity at a 90 percent threshold Used to cluster contigs into species-like viral OTUs.) and RCR90 (Reciprocal coverage ratio Ensures contigs belong to the same genome / species)

RVMT’s rule: Contigs belong to the same VOTU if RvANI90 ≥ 90% AND RCR90 ≥ 90%. These metrics are calculated, need to be converted into cluster IDs

viral <- readr::read_tsv("/work/pi_jlb_umass_edu/blanchardlab/RNA_phages/RVMT_Zenodo_V4/Expanded_Contig_Set/viral_contigs_annotated_full.tsv")

2 Rebuilding VOTUs from RCR90 and RvANI90 (VOTU ID for each contig)

7 identify treatment-specific VOTUs (anything in both is ignored)

genomes_per_votu_treat <- votu_rdrp |>
  group_by(Treatment, VOTU) |>
  summarize(GenomeCount = n_distinct(Contig), .groups = "drop")


votu_matrix <- genomes_per_votu_treat |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Treatment,
    values_from = GenomeCount,
    values_fill = 0
  )

Present in heated but absent in control

heated_only_count <- votu_matrix |>
  filter(C == 0 & H > 0) |>
  nrow()

heated_only_count
[1] 888

888 VOTUs exclusive to heated soils

Present in controls but absent in heated

control_only_count <- votu_matrix |>
  filter(H == 0 & C > 0) |>
  nrow()

control_only_count
[1] 1738

1738 VOTUs exclusive to control soils

Genome counts by treatment, reshape into long format for plotting and then plot counts per VOTU

votu_matrix <- genomes_per_votu_treat |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from = Treatment,
    values_from = GenomeCount,
    values_fill = 0
  )
votu_long <- votu_matrix |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(C, H), 
               names_to = "Treatment", 
               values_to = "GenomeCount")
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(votu_long, aes(x = Treatment, y = GenomeCount, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Genome Counts per VOTU in Heated vs Control Soils",
    x = "",
    y = "Genome Count"
  )
ggplot(votu_long, aes(x = Treatment, y = GenomeCount, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 10)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Genome Counts per VOTU (0–10)",
    x = "",
    y = "Genome Count"
  )
# 1-5 zoom 
ggplot(votu_long, aes(x = Treatment, y = GenomeCount, fill = Treatment)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 5)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Genome Counts per VOTU (Zoomed: 0–5)",
    x = "",
    y = "Genome Count"
  )

What this could mean :

Most VOTUs in both treatments have GenomeCount= 1. Most RNA virus “species” assemble into 1 contig.

Control VOTUs have more contigs per species.

Heated have far fewer extreme outliers highlighted in the 1-10 ??… Heated have no large clusters and Control has a small populaiton of complex VOTUs

# adding taxonomy to VOTUs 
votu_taxonomy <- votu_rdrp |>
  group_by(VOTU, Treatment) |>
  summarize(
    Orders = paste(unique(Order), collapse = "; "),
    Families = paste(unique(Family), collapse = "; "),
    Genera = paste(unique(Genus), collapse = "; "),
    GenomeCount = n_distinct(Contig),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

Median genomecount per phylum

med_gc <- votu_taxonomy2 |>
  group_by(Phylum, Treatment) |>
  summarize(
    median_gc = median(GenomeCount),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(med_gc, aes(
  x = Phylum,

Chi test do h v c differ in inflation structure?

tbl <- table(votu_taxonomy2$Treatment, votu_taxonomy2$GC_bin)
chisq.test(tbl)

    Pearson's Chi-squared test

data:  tbl
X-squared = 14.349, df = 3, p-value = 0.002467

pvalue of .002467. Highly significant. H vC do not produce VOTUS of the sane fragemntation

compare means/medians for typical genome count between treatments

wilcox.test(GenomeCount ~ Treatment, data = votu_taxonomy2)

    Wilcoxon rank sum test with continuity correction

data:  GenomeCount by Treatment
W = 1253972, p-value = 0.002714
alternative hypothesis: true location shift is not equal to 0

This could tell us that the typical genome assmebles differently under warming, heating reduces fragmentaiton (collapsing community) or increases highly framented VOTUs.

tail probalilties

  votu_taxonomy2$Treatment,
  votu_taxonomy2$GenomeCount > 5
)

chisq.test(tbl_tail)

    Pearson's Chi-squared test with Yates' continuity correction

data:  tbl_tail
X-squared = 9.4906, df = 1, p-value = 0.002065

Probanlity of a VOTU having fragmentation >5 is significantly different between treatments

Alluvial flow digram frgament flows

library(ggalluvial)

alluvial_df <- votu_taxonomy2 |>
  mutate(
    GC_bin = case_when(
      GenomeCount <= 1 ~ "1",
      GenomeCount <= 3 ~ "2–3",

    )
  )

ggplot(alluvial_df,
       aes(axis1 = Treatment, axis2 = GC_bin)) +
  geom_alluvium(aes(fill = GC_bin), width = 1/12) +
  geom_stratum(width = 1/12, fill = "grey90") +

  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Flow of VOTU Fragmentation Categories Between Treatments")

Thicker bands.. more VOTUs. Control has more VOTUS overall (2000ish) You can see wider ribbons flow into bins from control that have more fragments

cleaner version of flow

flow_df <- alluvial_df |>
  dplyr::count(Treatment, GC_bin, name = "Freq")

ggplot2::ggplot(
  flow_df,
  ggplot2::aes(axis1 = Treatment, axis2 = GC_bin, y = Freq)
) +

  ggalluvial::geom_alluvium(
    ggplot2::aes(fill = GC_bin),
    width = 0.25, alpha = 0.6, knot.pos = 0.4
  ) +

  ggalluvial::geom_stratum(
    width = 0.25, fill = "grey95", color = "black"
  ) +

  ggplot2::geom_label(
    stat = "stratum",
    ggplot2::aes(
      label = paste0(
        after_stat(stratum),
        "\n",
        round(after_stat(prop) * 100, 1), "%"
      )
    ),
    fill = "white", size = 4
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_x_discrete(
    limits = c("Treatment", "Fragmentation Bin"),
    expand = c(.05, .05)
  ) +

  ggplot2::scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "1" = "#A6D854",
    "2–3" = "#66C2A5",
    "4–6" = "#8DA0CB",
    ">6" = "#FC8D62"
  )) +

  ggplot2::labs(
    title = "Flow of VOTU Fragmentation Categories",
    y = "Number of VOTUs",
    x = "",
    fill = "Genome Count Bin"
  ) +

  ggplot2::theme_minimal(base_size = 15) +
  ggplot2::theme(
    axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
    panel.grid = ggplot2::element_blank()
  )

Limitation of the package is ribbons cant be labeled directly, only stratum labels

reassembly_candidates <- votu_rdrp |>
  dplyr::group_by(ND, VOTU) |>
  dplyr::summarize(n_contigs = dplyr::n_distinct(Contig), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n_contigs > 1)

  dplyr::summarize(n_contigs = dplyr::n_distinct(Contig), .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::filter(n_contigs > 1) |>
  dplyr::count(Treatment)

6 Unclassified             1.27      1.69      0.0298      0.0667
7 p.0002.base-Kitrino      9        NA         1          NA     
# ── 1. Aggregate to biological-sample level ─────────────────
# ND = one contig/detection, so we roll up to the true
# metagenome unit: Site × Subplot × Layer (Treatment follows)

votu_richness_meta <- votu_rdrp |>
  dplyr::group_by(Site, Subplot, Layer, Treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    VOTUrichness   = dplyr::n_distinct(VOTU),
    GenomeRichness = dplyr::n_distinct(Contig),
    .groups        = "drop"
  )

# Quick per-treatment summary
votu_richness_meta |>
  dplyr::group_by(Treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarize(
    n           = dplyr::n(),
    mean_VOTU   = mean(VOTUrichness),
    sd_VOTU     = sd(VOTUrichness),
    median_VOTU = median(VOTUrichness)
  )
# A tibble: 2 × 5
  Treatment     n mean_VOTU sd_VOTU median_VOTU
  <chr>     <int>     <dbl>   <dbl>       <dbl>
1 C            14      267    107.          255
2 H            14      178.    51.1         179
# ── 2. Normality check before choosing test ─────────────────
shapiro_C <- shapiro.test(
  votu_richness_meta$VOTUrichness[votu_richness_meta$Treatment == "C"]
)
shapiro_H <- shapiro.test(
  votu_richness_meta$VOTUrichness[votu_richness_meta$Treatment == "H"]
)

cat("Shapiro-Wilk  Control : W =", round(shapiro_C$statistic, 4),
    "  p =", round(shapiro_C$p.value, 4), "\n")
Shapiro-Wilk  Control : W = 0.9207   p = 0.2247 
cat("Shapiro-Wilk  Heated  : W =", round(shapiro_H$statistic, 4),
    "  p =", round(shapiro_H$p.value, 4), "\n")
Shapiro-Wilk  Heated  : W = 0.937   p = 0.381 
# p < 0.05 in either → favour the Wilcoxon fallback below

# ── 3. Welch two-sample t-test (primary) ────────────────────
# var.equal = FALSE (Welch correction) is safest for unequal n
ttest_votu <- t.test(
  VOTUrichness ~ Treatment,
  data      = votu_richness_meta,
  var.equal = FALSE
)
ttest_votu                   # full output

# ℹ 2 more variables: method <chr>, alternative <chr>
# ── 4. Non-parametric fallback ───────────────────────────────
# Use this if Shapiro-Wilk flags non-normality in either group
wilcox_votu <- wilcox.test(
  VOTUrichness ~ Treatment,
  data = votu_richness_meta
)

  p_val < 0.001 ~ "***",
  p_val < 0.01  ~ "**",
  p_val < 0.05  ~ "*",
  TRUE          ~ paste0("ns  (p = ", round(p_val, 3), ")")
)

y_max   <- max(votu_richness_meta$VOTUrichness, na.rm = TRUE)

  # ============================================================
# STEP 1: BUILD METAGENOME × VOTU ABUNDANCE MATRIX
# ============================================================

# 1a. Assign a unique ID to each biological metagenome
#     (Site + Subplot + Layer + Treatment = one soil core)
votu_rdrp_meta <- votu_rdrp |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(VOTU)) |>                        # drop missing VOTUs
  dplyr::mutate(
    SampleID = paste(Site, Subplot, Layer, Treatment, sep = "_")
  )

# 1b. Count distinct contigs per VOTU per metagenome (abundance)
votu_abund <- votu_rdrp_meta |>
  dplyr::group_by(SampleID, VOTU) |>
  dplyr::summarize(n_contigs = dplyr::n_distinct(Contig), .groups = "drop")

# 1c. Pivot to wide: rows = metagenomes, columns = VOTUs
votu_wide <- votu_abund |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(
    names_from  = VOTU,
    values_from = n_contigs,
    values_fill = 0
  )

# 1d. Pull sample metadata (one row per metagenome)
sample_meta <- votu_rdrp_meta |>
  dplyr::distinct(SampleID, Treatment, Site, Subplot, Layer)

# 1e. Numeric matrix with sample IDs as rownames
mat <- votu_wide |>
  tibble::column_to_rownames("SampleID") |>
  as.matrix()

# 1f. Align metadata rows to matrix row order — critical for vegan
meta_ordered <- sample_meta[match(rownames(mat), sample_meta$SampleID), ]

cat("Matrix:", nrow(mat), "metagenomes ×", ncol(mat), "VOTUs\n")
Matrix: 28 metagenomes × 2995 VOTUs

============================================================

STEP 2: DISSIMILARITY + STATISTICAL TESTS

============================================================

library(vegan)

# 2a. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity between every pair of metagenomes
#     Value of 0 = identical  |  Value of 1 = completely different
bc_dist <- vegan::vegdist(mat, method = "bray")

# ── PERMANOVA ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The proper multivariate test replacing a t-test here
# Question: does Treatment explain differences between metagenomes?
set.seed(42)
permanova_res <- vegan::adonis2(
  bc_dist ~ Treatment,
  data         = meta_ordered,
  permutations = 999
)
print(permanova_res)
Permutation test for adonis under reduced model
Terms added sequentially (first to last)
Permutation: free
Number of permutations: 999

vegan::adonis2(formula = bc_dist ~ Treatment, data = meta_ordered, permutations = 999)
          Df SumOfSqs      R2      F Pr(>F)    
Treatment  1   1.3725 0.13183 3.9479  0.001 ***
Residual  26   9.0386 0.86817                  
Total     27  10.4111 1.00000                  
---
Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
# R²  = proportion of variance explained by treatment
# p   < 0.05 = metagenomes differ significantly by treatment

# ── Betadisper ───────────────────────────────────────────────
# Tests whether within-group SPREAD differs between treatments
# Run this before trusting PERMANOVA — if significant, PERMANOVA
# may be detecting spread differences, not true community shifts
betadisp_res  <- vegan::betadisper(bc_dist, meta_ordered$Treatment)
betadisp_test <- permutest(betadisp_res, permutations = 999)
print(betadisp_test)

# Non-significant = equal spread = PERMANOVA result is reliable

STEP 4: PAIRWISE DISTANCE BOXPLOT WITH SIGNIFICANCE

============================================================

# 4a. Expand distance matrix to long format (upper triangle only)
dist_mat <- as.matrix(bc_dist)

pairs_df <- expand.grid(
  i = rownames(dist_mat),
  j = rownames(dist_mat),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  dplyr::filter(i < j) |>                              # avoid duplicates
  dplyr::mutate(
    Distance = dist_mat[cbind(i, j)],
    Treat_i  = meta_ordered$Treatment[match(i, meta_ordered$SampleID)],
    Treat_j  = meta_ordered$Treatment[match(j, meta_ordered$SampleID)],
    Comparison = factor(
      dplyr::case_when(
        Treat_i == "C" & Treat_j == "C" ~ "Within Control",
        Treat_i == "H" & Treat_j == "H" ~ "Within Heated",
        TRUE                             ~ "Between C & H"
      ),
      levels = c("Within Control", "Within Heated", "Between C & H")
    )
  )

# 4b. Welch t-tests between each pair of comparison groups
#     (direct vector approach avoids factor-level issues)
tt_WC_WH <- t.test(
  pairs_df$Distance[pairs_df$Comparison == "Within Control"],
  pairs_df$Distance[pairs_df$Comparison == "Within Heated"]
)
tt_WH_B <- t.test(
  pairs_df$Distance[pairs_df$Comparison == "Within Heated"],
  pairs_df$Distance[pairs_df$Comparison == "Between C & H"]
)
tt_WC_B <- t.test(
  pairs_df$Distance[pairs_df$Comparison == "Within Control"],
  pairs_df$Distance[pairs_df$Comparison == "Between C & H"]
)

# Star labels
p_star <- function(p) {
  if      (p < 0.001) "***"
  else if (p < 0.01)  "**"
  else if (p < 0.05)  "*"
  else                 "ns"
}

cat("Within Control vs Within Heated :",
    "t =", round(tt_WC_WH$statistic, 2),
    " p =", round(tt_WC_WH$p.value, 4),
    p_star(tt_WC_WH$p.value), "\n")
Within Control vs Within Heated : t = 4.14  p = 1e-04 *** 
cat("Within Heated  vs Between C & H :",
    "t =", round(tt_WH_B$statistic, 2),
    " p =", round(tt_WH_B$p.value, 4),
    p_star(tt_WH_B$p.value), "\n")
Within Heated  vs Between C & H : t = -14.23  p = 0 *** 
cat("Within Control vs Between C & H :",
    "t =", round(tt_WC_B$statistic, 2),
    " p =", round(tt_WC_B$p.value, 4),
    p_star(tt_WC_B$p.value), "\n")
Within Control vs Between C & H : t = -10.26  p = 0 ***
